intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on the night of the full moon when the streets are lit entirely by colorful silk lanterns. Rent a bicycle to roam the historic streets, visit tailor shops, and sample local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street stalls along the riverside.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic mountain roads connecting Da Nang and Hue. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of the coastline and lush jungle below.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, hopping on a traditional sampan boat through narrow canals lined with coconut palms. Visit floating markets, local cottage industries making rice paper and coconut candy, and sample tropical fruits straight from riverside orchards.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's backpacker scene on Bui Vien Street, a pedestrian-only strip buzzing with budget bars, live music, and street food stalls. Grab a plastic stool, order a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer for under $1), and soak in the electric atmosphere alongside fellow backpackers and locals.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow walk to orient yourself around Hoan Kiem Lake (15 min walk from most Old Quarter hostels). Stroll across the iconic red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (entrance ~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Dive straight into Old Quarter street food culture. Wander the 36 guild streets around Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) and Dinh Liet Street. Watch the evening buzz come alive with locals and backpackers. Grab a cheap bia hoi (draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) at a street-side plastic stool bar.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack on the plane.
meals.lunch: Grab a Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter upon arrival (~25,000–35,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local street stall on Hang Manh or Le Van Huu Street (~50,000–70,000 VND). Follow with a bia hoi on Ta Hien Street.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or use a local ATM in the Old Quarter. Avoid hotel exchange rates. Keep small bills handy for street food. Grab a local SIM card at the airport (Viettel or Mobifone, ~100,000–150,000 VND with data).

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a walk through the Old Quarter morning market scene. Visit Dong Xuan Market (Hanoi's largest covered market) — great for people-watching and cheap local snacks. Head to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free entry to grounds, mausoleum viewing is free but check opening hours — typically 7:30–10:30 AM Tue–Thu & Sat–Sun). Walk through Ba Dinh Square and view the Presidential Palace exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — one of Vietnam's most important historical sites (~30,000 VND entry). Spend 1.5 hours exploring the ancient Confucian university grounds, stone steles, and pavilions. Afterward, head to Hoa Lo Prison Museum (Hanoi Hilton, ~30,000 VND) for a sobering look at colonial and wartime history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday evenings, free to browse). Shop for souvenirs, street snacks, and handmade goods. End the night with egg coffee (ca phe trung) at Cafe Giang, a Hanoi institution (~25,000–40,000 VND).

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at a local street pho stall near the hotel (~40,000–60,000 VND). Look for places with plastic stools packed with locals.
meals.lunch: Bun Oc (snail noodle soup) or Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a street vendor near Temple of Literature (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric grilled fish with dill) — splurge slightly at a local restaurant on Cha Ca Street (~80,000–120,000 VND). A Hanoi must-eat.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and during October–November for maintenance. Verify schedule before going. Dress modestly for temple and mausoleum visits. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 6–8 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Join the locals for morning Tai Chi at Hoan Kiem Lake (free, starts around 6:00–7:00 AM — a magical cultural experience). Afterward, explore the quieter backstreets of the Old Quarter on foot. Visit the Bach Ma Temple (White Horse Temple) on Hang Buom Street — one of Hanoi's oldest temples (free or small donation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry, 15 min by taxi ~60,000 VND or grab a xe om motorbike taxi). One of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums with outdoor traditional house displays from 54 ethnic groups. Return to the Old Quarter by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (~100,000 VND for standard seats — book at the box office in person). A uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back 1,000 years. Afterward, explore the vibrant Luong Ngoc Quyen backpacker street for evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street cart near Hoan Kiem Lake (~20,000–30,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (budget rice plate with multiple toppings) near the Museum of Ethnology (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Nem Cuon (fresh spring rolls) and Pho Cuon (rolled pho) at a casual restaurant on Ngu Xa Street, West Lake area (~50,000–80,000 VND total).

day_by_day.notes: The Water Puppet Show runs multiple times daily — the 18:00 or 20:00 shows are most convenient. Book tickets in person earlier in the day to guarantee seats on weekends. The Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh! Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station (~70,000–90,000 VND, ~2 hours). Alternatively, book a budget day tour from the Old Quarter (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) to explore the Tam Coc valley. Cycle through rice paddies and karst limestone scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a rowboat through the Tam Coc caves (~150,000 VND per boat, fits 2 people — a 2-hour scenic river journey through three natural caves). Visit Bich Dong Pagoda (free), a stunning pagoda built into a limestone cliff. Explore the surrounding countryside on bicycle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus (~90,000 VND). Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 19:00–20:00. Decompress with a light dinner and early rest to prepare for the next leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street stall near the bus station before departure (~25,000–35,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Ninh Binh town — Com Rang (fried rice) or goat meat (de nui), a Ninh Binh specialty (~60,000–100,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Simple bowl of Mien Ga (glass noodle chicken soup) or Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) from a street stall near the hotel (~40,000–60,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is often called 'Ha Long Bay on land' — absolutely worth the day trip. Start as early as 7:00 AM to beat the midday heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light rain jacket. The rowboat ladies often expect a tip for their extraordinary rowing technique (using their feet!).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the overnight train or early morning bus from Hanoi to Hue. The train (SE3 or similar, soft seat ~200,000–300,000 VND or sleeper ~350,000–500,000 VND) is the most scenic and budget-friendly option. Book tickets at Hanoi Railway Station or online via Vietnam Railways. Depart by 7:00–9:00 AM. Enjoy the stunning coastal scenery as the train hugs the central Vietnamese coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hue in the late afternoon (~13:00–16:00 depending on train). Check in to a budget guesthouse in the Pham Ngu Lao or Nguyen Tri Phuong area (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Take a slow walk along the Perfume River (Song Huong) to shake off the journey. Visit the imposing Imperial Citadel exterior (save full entry for tomorrow morning).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hue's famous street food scene around Dong Ba Market and the surrounding streets. Hue is considered the culinary capital of Vietnam — every dish here is a cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi near Hanoi Railway Station before departure (~35,000–50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Snacks or packed food on the train — buy from platform vendors at station stops (~20,000–40,000 VND for instant noodles, boiled eggs, or snacks).
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) at a street stall near Dong Ba Market — the authentic version, not the watered-down tourist variety (~40,000–60,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: The Hanoi–Hue train journey is one of the great rail experiences in Southeast Asia, especially the Hai Van Pass section. Try to get a window seat on the right side of the train (when heading south) for the best coastal views. Confirm your guesthouse booking in advance for Hue.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Hue's Imperial Citadel and Forbidden Purple City (~200,000 VND entry). Explore the vast royal complex, ornate gates, royal theatre (Duyet Thi Duong), and the partially restored Forbidden City. Allow 2–3 hours minimum. The scale and history are extraordinary — this was the seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) or hire a xe om to visit the Royal Tombs south of the city. The Tomb of Tu Duc (~100,000 VND) is the most picturesque — a romantic, poetic complex built by the emperor himself. Also visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free) on the banks of the Perfume River — Hue's most iconic religious landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center. Walk across Truong Tien Bridge at sunset for beautiful river views. Explore the night market on Pham Ngu Lao Street (Hue's backpacker strip). Try Hue's famous royal cuisine snacks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake with shrimp and pork, dipped in peanut sauce) from a street stall (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) or Bun Hen (clam noodles) — a uniquely Hue dish found near Dong Ba Market (~25,000–40,000 VND). Humble but deeply flavorful.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Hue or a set meal at a local com binh dan restaurant near the guesthouse (~50,000–80,000 VND). Try Che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup) for dessert (~15,000–20,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: April in Hue can be hot and occasionally rainy — carry a small umbrella or light rain poncho. The Royal Tombs are spread out — a bicycle works well but a xe om is faster if time is short. Bargain politely for xe om prices before getting on.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early bus or train from Hue to Hoi An via Da Nang (~2.5–3.5 hours, ~100,000–150,000 VND by bus or shared minivan). The route crosses the legendary Hai Van Pass — if taking a bus, some stop for photos at the top. Arrive in Hoi An and check in to a budget guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town (~150,000–250,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hoi An Ancient Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Buy a combined entrance ticket (~120,000 VND, covers 5 heritage sites). Visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), Tan Ky Old House, and Phuc Kien Assembly Hall. Wander the beautifully preserved yellow-walled streets.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An Ancient Town transforms magically at night with thousands of silk lanterns. Walk along the Thu Bon River, watch lanterns float on the water, and soak in the romantic atmosphere. Browse the lantern and silk shops. The town is most beautiful after dark.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or sticky rice before departure from Hue (~25,000–35,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and greens) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~50,000–70,000 VND). Authentic Cao Lau uses water from a specific local well — only available in Hoi An.
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Hoi An Fried Wontons (Hoành Thánh Chien) at a street stall or small restaurant near the river (~60,000–90,000 VND total).

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely walkable — leave your motorbike or bicycle at the guesthouse when exploring the Ancient Town core (some areas are pedestrian-only). The combined heritage ticket is valid for multiple days. Lantern Festival happens on the 14th of each lunar month — check if it falls during your stay for an extraordinary experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxed morning by the sea. Swim, read, and enjoy the relative quiet of the morning before day-trippers arrive. This is one of the most beautiful stretches of central Vietnamese coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to the Tra Que Vegetable Village (~3 km from town) — a charming organic farming community. Join a short cooking class or farming experience (~150,000–250,000 VND) where you learn to make traditional Hoi An dishes using freshly harvested herbs and vegetables. Alternatively, visit the My Son Sanctuary (Hindu Cham ruins, ~150,000 VND entry + transport) for a half-day trip — book a shared tour from your guesthouse (~100,000–150,000 VND transport).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town for a final evening stroll. Visit the Hoi An Night Market on An Hoi Island (cross the footbridge). Browse handmade crafts, lanterns, and street food. Splurge slightly on a tailored item if interested — Hoi An is famous for 24-hour custom tailoring at budget prices.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (Quang Nam-style turmeric noodles with pork, shrimp, and herbs) from a street stall near your guesthouse (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beach shack at An Bang Beach — grilled fish or prawns (~80,000–120,000 VND). Slightly pricier but worth the beachside experience.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong — the most famous Banh Mi in Vietnam (featured by Anthony Bourdain), located at 2B Phan Chau Trinh (~35,000–45,000 VND). Then grab a Hoi An specialty dessert: Banh Dap (crispy rice crackers with wet rice paper) (~20,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Banh Mi Phuong often has a queue — go early (before 18:00) or be prepared to wait. The tailoring shops in Hoi An can produce quality custom clothing in 24–48 hours at very reasonable prices — bring inspiration photos if interested. Negotiate respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or sleeper bus from Hoi An/Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). The overnight bus option (~250,000–350,000 VND, ~18 hours) is the most budget-friendly but long. Alternatively, fly Da Nang to HCMC (~500,000–900,000 VND on VietJet or Bamboo Airways — book in advance for best prices). Flying is recommended to save time. Depart by 8:00–10:00 AM flight to arrive in HCMC by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City. Take a bus or Grab (ride-hailing app) from Tan Son Nhat Airport to the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district (~50,000–80,000 VND by Grab). Check in to a budget guesthouse or hostel (~120,000–200,000 VND/night). Head straight to the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND entry) — one of the most powerful and important museums in Southeast Asia. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area — the beating heart of budget travel in HCMC. Walk to Ben Thanh Market (closes around 18:00 for the indoor market, but street food stalls open until late outside). Experience the electric energy of Saigon at night — motorbikes, neon lights, and street food everywhere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Banh Mi or bowl of noodles near your Hoi An guesthouse before departure (~25,000–40,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Airport snack or food court meal in Da Nang airport (~60,000–100,000 VND) or first meal in HCMC upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) or Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at a street stall in Pham Ngu Lao (~50,000–70,000 VND). Com Tam is the quintessential Saigon dish.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Da Nang to HCMC flight well in advance for the best budget fares on VietJet Air or Bamboo Airways. Install the Grab app before arriving in HCMC — it's far cheaper and safer than street taxis. The War Remnants Museum is intense and emotionally heavy — allow time to process it.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace, ~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, left exactly as it was on April 30, 1975. Fascinating Cold War-era architecture and history. Walk to Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (exterior viewing, currently under renovation) and the Central Post Office (free to enter — stunning French colonial architecture designed by Gustave Eiffel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~60–70 km from HCMC). Book a shared budget tour from Pham Ngu Lao (~150,000–200,000 VND including transport and entry). Crawl through the legendary underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the Vietnam War. An extraordinary and humbling historical experience. Return to HCMC by 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — celebrate your 10-day journey! Head to Bui Vien Walking Street (HCMC's famous backpacker party street) for cheap drinks, live music, and a festive atmosphere. Alternatively, for a more authentic local experience, grab a plastic stool at a bia hoi on Ly Tu Trong Street and watch Saigon's nightlife unfold around you.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (Vietnamese-style fried egg Banh Mi with pate and cold cuts) from a street cart near your guesthouse (~25,000–35,000 VND). A classic Saigon breakfast.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Cu Chi Tunnels site restaurant or packed snacks (~50,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your final meal: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) at a local restaurant near Pham Ngu Lao (~120,000–180,000 VND per person) or a full Com Tam spread with all the trimmings (~70,000–100,000 VND). End with a Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da, ~25,000–35,000 VND) — the perfect farewell to Vietnam.

day_by_day.notes: The Cu Chi Tunnels tour is a highlight of any Vietnam trip — don't skip it. The Ben Duoc site is less touristy than Ben Dinh and is recommended for a more authentic experience. Pack light for the tunnels — no large bags. If you have an early departure flight tomorrow, arrange airport transport the night before via Grab or ask your guesthouse. Keep some VND for last-minute street food and tips.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Quarter boutique hotel (~45 min by taxi or airport bus). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a map of the Old Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walk through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the bustling lanes nearby. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and admire the Turtle Tower from the lakeside promenade. Pop into Ngoc Son Temple on the lake island (small entrance fee ~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday evenings) for souvenir browsing and street snacks. Settle into a plastic-stool bia hoi (street beer) corner near Ta Hien Street — the famous 'Beer Corner' — for cold local draft beer and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or grab a quick bánh mì from a street cart near the hotel upon arrival (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Phở Bò at a local Old Quarter pho shop such as Phở Gia Truyền on Bat Dan Street — a Hanoi institution (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bún Chả at Bún Chả Hương Liên (the 'Obama Bun Cha' spot on Le Van Huu) — grilled pork patties with vermicelli noodles (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: April in Hanoi is warm and humid (~28–32°C). Light clothing recommended. Exchange some USD to VND at the hotel or a nearby exchange booth. Grab a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data (~150,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex early (open 7:30–10:30 AM, closed Mon/Fri). See the One Pillar Pagoda and Ho Chi Minh Museum nearby. Walk through Ba Dinh Square and admire the Presidential Palace gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, dating to 1070. Spend time reading the stone steles and exploring the serene courtyards (~30,000 VND entry). Afterward, stroll through the nearby Dong Da district and visit a local café for Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre on Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND, book ahead). Afterward, dinner in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Xôi Xéo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street vendor near the hotel (~25,000–40,000 VND) + Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Bánh Cuốn (steamed rice rolls) at a local spot in the Old Quarter (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Chả Cá Lã Vọng — Hanoi's famous turmeric-marinated grilled fish with dill — at the original restaurant on Cha Ca Street (~180,000–220,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum is closed Monday and Friday and during the annual maintenance period (Sept–Nov). Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered. Water puppet show lasts about 50 minutes; evening shows at 18:00, 19:30, and 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (~2 hours south by bus or organized tour). Rent a bicycle or rowboat at Tam Coc and explore the stunning karst limestone landscape along the Ngo Dong River. Pass through rice paddies and cave tunnels carved by the river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bich Dong Pagoda — a scenic cave pagoda carved into the mountainside (~15,000 VND). Optionally hike up to the viewpoint above for panoramic valley views. Explore Hoa Lu Ancient Capital, the 10th-century royal citadel with ornate temples (~20,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by early evening. Relax at a rooftop bar in the Old Quarter such as Skyline Bar or Note Coffee for sunset views over the city's rooftops.

meals.breakfast: Bánh Mì Pate from a street cart near the hotel (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh goat meat or fish dishes at a local Ninh Binh restaurant near Tam Coc (~80,000–120,000 VND) — the region is famous for its goat cuisine
meals.dinner: Lẩu (Vietnamese hot pot) at a mid-range restaurant in the Old Quarter, shared style (~150,000–200,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book a Ninh Binh day tour through your hotel or Hanoi travel agencies (~250,000–400,000 VND including transport). Alternatively, take the public bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat station. Bring sunscreen and a hat — the boat ride is exposed to sun.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi by sleeper bus or train to Hue (~12–14 hours by overnight train, or fly for ~1 hour). If taking the morning train (e.g., SE3 departing ~06:00), enjoy the scenic Hai Van Pass coastal route. Alternatively, book a budget flight (check Vietjet/Bamboo) and arrive by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hue's city center. Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Kinh Thanh) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Forbidden Purple City ruins, the Flag Tower, and the ornate Ngo Mon Gate (~200,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River promenade at sunset. Explore Dong Ba Market for local crafts and street snacks. Enjoy dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Grab food at Hanoi train station or on board — instant noodles or station bánh mì (~20,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bún Bò Huế — Hue's iconic spicy beef noodle soup — at a local eatery near the citadel (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cơm Hến (baby clam rice) and Bánh Khoái (Hue crispy pancake) at a local Hue restaurant near Dong Ba Market (~80,000–120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The overnight SE train from Hanoi to Hue costs ~300,000–500,000 VND for a soft sleeper berth — book in advance at dsvn.vn or through your hotel. Flying saves time (~700,000–1,200,000 VND). April weather in Hue can be warm and occasionally rainy — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike or join a guided tour to explore Hue's Royal Tombs. Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc (most elaborate, set in a pine forest) and the Tomb of Minh Mang (symmetrical gardens). Each tomb ~100,000–150,000 VND entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's iconic seven-story pagoda perched on the Perfume River — accessible by boat or motorbike (free entry). Continue to the Hue Royal Antiquities Museum at Long An Palace (~40,000 VND) to see imperial artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Book a dragon boat cruise on the Perfume River at sunset (~150,000–200,000 VND per person). Includes live traditional Nha Nhac court music performance. Dinner back in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Bánh Bèo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) at a local Hue breakfast stall (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style snacks from street vendors near the tombs, or lunch at a simple local restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Royal Hue cuisine set menu at a mid-range restaurant such as Tinh Gia Vien or Les Jardins de la Carambole (~200,000–300,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a motorbike in Hue costs ~120,000–150,000 VND/day. The tombs are spread out — a motorbike or bicycle is the most flexible option. Combine 2–3 tombs in one ticket for savings. Nha Nhac music is a UNESCO Intangible Heritage — a unique cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Hue to Hoi An (~3 hours by bus or private transfer, ~130 km). The route crosses the spectacular Hai Van Pass — consider renting a motorbike for this leg for the full scenic experience. Stop at Lang Co Beach for a short break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in or near Hoi An Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot: visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung Old House, and the Assembly Halls of the Chinese congregations (~120,000 VND combined ticket for 5 sites).
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Ancient Town as the lanterns light up at dusk — the most magical time in Hoi An. Browse the night market on An Hoi Island. Join a cooking class or lantern-making workshop (~200,000–350,000 VND).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Bánh Mì from a street cart in Hue before departure
meals.lunch: Cao Lầu — Hoi An's signature noodle dish made with local well water — at Cao Lau Thanh in the Ancient Town (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Bánh Vạc) and Hoi An specialties at a riverside restaurant in the Ancient Town (~120,000–180,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Hue–Hoi An bus (open-tour style) costs ~100,000–200,000 VND. Private transfer is ~600,000–800,000 VND for a car. The Hai Van Pass motorbike ride is one of Vietnam's most celebrated road experiences — only recommended for confident riders. Hoi An Ancient Town entry ticket covers 5 attractions of your choice.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle and ride to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from the Ancient Town) for a relaxed morning swim and beach walk. April is generally a good beach month in Hoi An before the rainy season.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the My Son Sanctuary (~45 min from Hoi An by motorbike or tour) — ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins in a jungle valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (~150,000 VND entry). Explore the moss-covered towers and learn about the Cham civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An. Take a Vietnamese cooking class in the evening that includes a visit to the local market (~400,000–600,000 VND — many reputable schools offer this). Learn to make Cao Lau, White Rose, and fresh spring rolls.

meals.breakfast: Bánh Mì Phượng — arguably Vietnam's most famous bánh mì shop on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~35,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside shack at An Bang Beach — grilled prawns, clams, and cold beer (~100,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked in your cooking class, or dine at a lantern-lit riverside restaurant in the Ancient Town (~100,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: My Son tours depart in the morning (~7:30 AM) — consider booking the afternoon session instead to avoid the midday heat and tour groups. Bicycle rental in Hoi An costs ~50,000–80,000 VND/day. Hoi An is very walkable and cycling-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Da Nang Airport (30 min from Hoi An) to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Book an early morning flight (~1 hour, ~700,000–1,500,000 VND on Vietjet or Bamboo). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in the Bui Vien/Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district or District 1.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum — a powerful and sobering museum documenting the Vietnam War (~40,000 VND). Walk to Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) nearby — preserved exactly as it was in 1975 (~40,000 VND). Stroll through April 30 Park.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker strip. Enjoy the lively atmosphere, street food stalls, and live music. Take a walk along Nguyen Hue Boulevard — the city's grand pedestrian boulevard lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Airport or hotel breakfast, or grab a quick snack before the flight
meals.lunch: Cơm Tấm (broken rice with grilled pork, egg, and pickles) at a local HCMC eatery — a Saigon staple (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl on Bui Vien Street — try Bánh Tráng Nướng (grilled rice paper 'Vietnamese pizza'), grilled skewers, and fresh sugarcane juice (~80,000–120,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Transfer from Hoi An to Da Nang Airport by taxi (~250,000–350,000 VND, ~30–40 min). Book the flight at least a few days in advance. HCMC is bigger and busier than Hanoi — use Grab (ride-hailing app) for affordable, reliable transport around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km northwest of HCMC) — the legendary underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the war. Join a half-day tour (departs ~7:30 AM, returns by noon, ~200,000–350,000 VND including transport). Crawl through the tunnels and see wartime exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC. Visit Ben Thanh Market for souvenir shopping and street food grazing. Explore the surrounding streets: Ly Tu Trong, Nam Ky Khoi Nghia for French colonial architecture. Stop into the stunning Saigon Central Post Office and Notre-Dame Cathedral (exterior viewing during renovation).
day_by_day.evening: Explore District 3 or District 4 for a more local HCMC experience. Visit a rooftop bar such as Chill Skybar or Saigon Saigon Rooftop Bar for city views. End the evening with a bowl of late-night street noodles.

meals.breakfast: Bánh Cuốn or Hủ Tiếu (Southern-style noodle soup) from a local breakfast stall near the hotel (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Snacks and street food at Ben Thanh Market food stalls upon return (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a local District 4 seafood alley — try grilled scallops with peanuts, clams in lemongrass, and grilled squid (~150,000–200,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels tours can be booked through your hotel or any District 1 travel agency. The Ben Dinh site is less touristy than Ben Duoc — worth specifying. Drink plenty of water — HCMC in April is hot (~33–36°C) and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day Mekong Delta tour from HCMC — visit My Tho or Ben Tre province by speedboat. Explore floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and fruit orchards. Row through narrow mangrove canals on a sampan boat. (~400,000–600,000 VND for a day tour including transport and lunch).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by mid-afternoon. Final souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the artisan shops along Dong Khoi Street. Visit the HCMC Museum (~30,000 VND) for a final overview of the city's history. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in HCMC — treat yourself to a slightly elevated meal at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant. Reflect on the journey. Transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport if departing tonight, or relax at a rooftop café.

meals.breakfast: Phở or Bún Bò from a local morning stall near the hotel (~50,000–70,000 VND) — compare Saigon-style pho (sweeter broth) to Hanoi's version
meals.lunch: Included in the Mekong Delta tour — typically a set meal of river fish, fresh spring rolls, and tropical fruit (~included or ~80,000–100,000 VND supplement)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cục Gạch Quán (rustic Vietnamese home-style cuisine in a charming colonial villa, District 3) or a similar mid-range restaurant (~200,000–300,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mekong Delta day tours from HCMC are widely available — book through your hotel or a reputable agency like Sinh Tourist or Mekong Eyes. If departing late, store luggage at the hotel. Tan Son Nhat Airport is ~30–45 min from District 1 by Grab taxi (~120,000–180,000 VND). Allow 2.5–3 hours before international departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the iconic 36 Streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Explore the labyrinthine lanes, admire French colonial architecture, and soak in the vibrant street life. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the historic Ngoc Son Temple on Jade Island — a serene introduction to Hanoi's soul.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along Hoan Kiem Lake promenade, then head to the famous Hanoi Weekend Night Market (open Fri–Sun) or explore Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Street' — for an authentic local atmosphere. Wind down with a premium dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at Chả Cá Thăng Long — a Hanoi institution famous for its sizzling turmeric fish served tableside with dill and vermicelli noodles.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane (French-Vietnamese fusion) or Cha Ca La Vong for a refined yet authentic Hanoi culinary experience. Pair with a Vietnamese craft cocktail at Polite Pub rooftop bar.

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH arrives 13:00. Arrange private airport transfer in advance. April in Hanoi is warm (26–32°C) with occasional light showers — pack a light rain jacket. No activities before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hoan Kiem Lake for a peaceful walk among locals doing tai chi and morning exercises — a quintessential Hanoi experience. Proceed to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first national university built in 1070, for a deep dive into Vietnamese Confucian heritage. Hire a private guide for enriched storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology — one of Southeast Asia's finest museums — showcasing the country's 54 ethnic groups through immersive exhibits and outdoor reconstructed village houses. Afterward, visit the iconic Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and the Presidential Palace gardens (check opening hours in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Experience the legendary Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre for a traditional performance rooted in 11th-century Red River Delta culture. Post-show, explore the Old Quarter's atmospheric night scene and enjoy a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) breakfast at Pho Thin — a legendary Hanoi pho institution open since 1979, beloved by locals and culinary travelers alike.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Obama at Bun Cha Huong Lien — the famous spot where Anthony Bourdain and President Obama dined together in 2016. A must-do Hanoi cultural moment.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Maison Vie — a sophisticated rooftop restaurant in the Old Quarter offering elevated Vietnamese cuisine with panoramic city views.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and for approximately two months annually (usually Sept–Nov) for maintenance — verify dates. Dress modestly for temple and mausoleum visits. Book water puppet theatre tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to Ha Long Bay — one of the world's most breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Depart Hanoi by private luxury vehicle (approximately 3.5 hours). Board a premium overnight junk cruise (Heritage Line or Indochine Sails recommended). Sail through dramatic limestone karsts, enjoy welcome drinks and a cooking demonstration on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through hidden lagoons and sea caves, including the spectacular Luon Cave and Bright Cave. Swim in emerald waters in a secluded cove. Visit a traditional floating fishing village for a glimpse into centuries-old maritime life. Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the karst landscape glows golden.
day_by_day.evening: Gourmet seafood dinner aboard the cruise ship — freshly caught squid, prawns, and fish prepared by the onboard chef. Squid fishing off the deck under the stars. Overnight on the bay in a luxuriously appointed cabin.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at hotel before departure or a packed premium breakfast box provided by the hotel.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch served aboard the cruise — Vietnamese-style steamed fish, spring rolls, and local vegetables with rice.
meals.dinner: Five-course gourmet dinner aboard the junk cruise featuring fresh Ha Long Bay seafood, Vietnamese delicacies, and paired wines.

day_by_day.notes: Book a premium overnight cruise well in advance — Heritage Line Ylang or Indochine Sails are among the finest operators. Bring sunscreen, swimwear, and a light jacket for evening breezes on the water. This is a 2-day/1-night excursion returning the following afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up on Ha Long Bay to a stunning sunrise over the karsts. Morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck, followed by a final kayaking excursion or cave exploration before breakfast. Enjoy a leisurely brunch aboard as the cruise returns to the harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and private luxury transfer back to Hanoi (approximately 3.5 hours). Upon return, check back into Old Quarter hotel and refresh. Optional: visit the Hanoi Ceramic Road (Con De Street) — a 4km mosaic mural stretching along the Red River dyke, a remarkable public art landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Dong Xuan Market — Hanoi's largest covered market — for local crafts, textiles, and street food. Enjoy a premium street food walking tour of the Old Quarter with a private culinary guide, sampling banh mi, nem ran, and banh cuon from the best hidden vendors.

meals.breakfast: Brunch aboard the Ha Long Bay cruise — dim sum, fresh fruit, Vietnamese congee, and eggs to order.
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route back to Hanoi or at a recommended roadside restaurant in Hai Duong province.
meals.dinner: Curated premium street food tour dinner — multiple tastings across Old Quarter vendors. End the evening with a nightcap at Hanoi Social Club, a beloved bohemian bar with craft cocktails and live music.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer with cruise operator. April weather on Ha Long Bay is generally warm and pleasant. The Ceramic Road is best appreciated on foot or by bicycle — rentals available near the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Hanoi (HAN) to Hue (HUI) — approximately 1 hour. Private luxury transfer to your premium hotel in Hue (La Residence Hotel & Spa recommended — a beautifully restored French Governor's residence on the Perfume River). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive visit to the Hue Imperial Citadel — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Forbidden Purple City, the Nine Dynastic Urns, and the ornate royal pavilions with a private expert guide. Afterward, visit the serene Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's most iconic Buddhist landmark — perched above the Perfume River.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dragon boat cruise along the Perfume River, listening to Hue's hauntingly beautiful Nha Nhac court music performed live by traditional musicians — a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage experience. Disembark for a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a legendary Old Quarter vendor before heading to the airport, or breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a renowned local restaurant — considered by many to surpass even Hanoi pho in complexity and depth.
meals.dinner: Royal Hue cuisine dinner at Les Jardins de la Carambole — an elegant French colonial villa restaurant serving meticulously crafted imperial Vietnamese dishes in a garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book morning flights in advance. Hue is the culinary heartland of Vietnam — every meal here should be treated as a cultural experience. Dress modestly for temple and citadel visits. The dragon boat cruise should be pre-arranged through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to the Royal Tombs of the Nguyen Emperors — visit the spectacular tomb complexes of Emperor Tu Duc and Emperor Minh Mang, set in pine-forested hills outside Hue. Each tomb is an architectural masterpiece blending Vietnamese, Chinese, and French influences. Explore with a knowledgeable private historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Thuy Xuan — Hue's famous incense-making village — where artisans craft colorful incense sticks using traditional methods. Participate in a hands-on incense-making workshop. Continue to a traditional Hue conical hat (Non La) workshop for a cultural craft demonstration. Drive the legendary Hai Van Pass for panoramic coastal views before descending to Da Nang.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Da Nang. Check into a luxury beachfront resort on My Khe Beach (InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula or Naman Retreat recommended). Enjoy the resort's facilities, a beach walk at sunset, and a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancakes with shrimp and pork) at a beloved local eatery near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) — Hue's iconic humble dish — at a riverside local restaurant, a must-try for street food enthusiasts.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant or at Ngu Hanh Son — a premium seafood restaurant in Da Nang with views of the Marble Mountains.

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass drive is spectacular but adds time — factor this into your schedule. A private driver is strongly recommended for this day. Check resort check-in times and arrange transfers accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on Da Nang's pristine My Khe Beach — one of the world's most beautiful beaches. Optional sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort. After breakfast, visit the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) — a cluster of five limestone and marble hills with ancient Buddhist sanctuaries, caves, and panoramic views of the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Half-day excursion to the ancient trading port of Hoi An (30 minutes from Da Nang) — a UNESCO World Heritage town frozen in time. Explore the Japanese Covered Bridge, the Assembly Halls of Chinese merchants, and the lantern-lit Old Town streets. Visit a premium tailor for a bespoke ao dai or suit fitting (Hoi An is world-famous for its skilled tailors).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hoi An for the evening — the town transforms magically at night with thousands of silk lanterns. Join a premium cooking class with a master chef, learning to prepare authentic Hoi An specialties. Afterward, enjoy dinner at the cooking school or a riverside restaurant, then browse the lantern market.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet featuring Vietnamese and international options with ocean views.
meals.lunch: Cao Lau — Hoi An's signature dish of thick noodles, pork, and crispy croutons, uniquely made with water from a specific local well — at Thanh Cao Lau, a beloved institution.
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner at Red Bridge Cooking School or The Morning Glory Restaurant — an elevated Hoi An dining institution run by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy.

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Old Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Avoid peak midday heat by scheduling outdoor exploration in early afternoon. If ordering bespoke tailoring, allow 24–48 hours for alterations — plan a return visit on Day 8.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hoi An in the morning for a private guided bicycle tour through the lush countryside surrounding the ancient town — rice paddies, vegetable farms, and traditional villages. Visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village, where local farmers use ancient organic techniques, and participate in a farm-to-table gardening experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Collect bespoke tailored items from Hoi An tailors. Explore the My Son Sanctuary — a cluster of abandoned and partially ruined Hindu temples constructed between the 4th and 14th centuries by the Cham civilization, set in a lush jungle valley (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Return to Da Nang resort for a relaxing afternoon at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa treatment at the resort (signature Vietnamese herbal therapy or hot stone massage recommended). Sunset cocktails at the resort's infinity pool bar overlooking the South China Sea. Premium farewell dinner to the Central Vietnam leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — widely considered the world's best banh mi, as declared by Anthony Bourdain — at the original stall in Hoi An.
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Fried Wonton at White Rose Restaurant — a Hoi An exclusive dish made by a single family for generations.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant or at Waterfront Restaurant & Bar in Da Nang — a sophisticated riverside venue with an extensive wine list and premium Vietnamese-international menu.

day_by_day.notes: My Son Sanctuary is approximately 40km from Hoi An — arrange private transport. The site involves walking on uneven terrain; wear comfortable shoes. Book spa treatments in advance as premium slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Da Nang (DAD) to Ho Chi Minh City (SGN) — approximately 1 hour 15 minutes. Private luxury transfer to your premium hotel in Ho Chi Minh City (Park Hyatt Saigon or The Reverie Saigon recommended, located in District 1). Check in, freshen up, and begin exploring Vietnam's dynamic southern metropolis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive cultural tour of Ho Chi Minh City's historic landmarks: the War Remnants Museum (sobering and essential), the Reunification Palace (former South Vietnamese presidential palace), the ornate Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon, and the Central Post Office — a stunning French colonial masterpiece designed by Gustave Eiffel. Private guide recommended for historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Market area and the surrounding streets for an authentic Saigon street food experience. Then head to the rooftop bar of the Chill Skybar or The Social Club Rooftop for panoramic city views and craft cocktails as Ho Chi Minh City lights up below.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast aboard the flight or a quick Banh Mi from a street vendor near the Da Nang hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style noodle soup) — a Saigon street food staple — at a well-regarded local restaurant in District 5 (Cholon, Saigon's Chinatown).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuc Gach Quan — a beloved Saigon restaurant housed in a beautifully restored villa, serving rustic Vietnamese home-cooking elevated to an art form. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City traffic can be intense — factor in extra travel time. A private driver for the full day is strongly recommended. The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allow adequate time and mental preparation.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to the Mekong Delta — the 'rice bowl' of Vietnam. Depart by private vehicle to My Tho or Ben Tre (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Board a private boat to explore the labyrinthine waterways, floating markets, and lush river islands. Visit a coconut candy workshop, a traditional rice paper factory, and a honey bee farm. Cycle through sleepy villages on unpaved paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat cruise deeper into the delta, stopping at a floating market to witness the chaotic beauty of river commerce. Enjoy a riverside lunch at a local family home. Return to Ho Chi Minh City by private vehicle. Upon return, visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda — one of Saigon's most atmospheric and ornate temples — and stroll through the French Quarter of District 1.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — a premium farewell experience. Enjoy a private rooftop dinner at The Reverie Saigon's Café Cardinal or a chef's table experience at Anan Saigon — Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's celebrated modern Vietnamese restaurant that reimagines street food through a fine-dining lens. End the evening with a nightcap at a jazz bar or the iconic Apocalypse Now bar for a final taste of Saigon's legendary nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast at your Ho Chi Minh City property — Vietnamese and international spread with fresh tropical fruits.
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta feast at a riverside family home — elephant ear fish (Ca Tai Tuong), fresh spring rolls, and local river prawns cooked in coconut water.
meals.dinner: Chef's table or tasting menu dinner at Anan Saigon — one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants — featuring inventive Vietnamese cuisine with premium wine pairing. A perfect culinary finale to the journey.

day_by_day.notes: This is the final full day — pack bags the evening before if departing early the next morning. Confirm return flight details and arrange a private luxury airport transfer. Anan Saigon requires advance reservations — book at least 2 weeks ahead. Tipping etiquette: 10–15% is appreciated at premium restaurants in Vietnam.
